newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices track foreign markets up.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices track foreign markets up.

text.p: Danish bond prices followed foreign markets upward on Friday, in the wake of a speech by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan which lowered expectations of an imminent U.S. rate cut.
"It is a wonderful market, pushed from abroad. The central bank is by and large the only seller of government bonds today," a dealer said.

At 1125 GMT the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.63 point from Wednesdays' close, to 111.08, yielding 6.32 percent, in turnover of 3.5 billion crowns. Its June future rose 0.45 point to 110.50 with 256 contracts traded.
The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.55 point, to 88.70.
The crown traded at 3.8071 per mark, unmoved from its opening price. The 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed to 59 basis points from an earlier 64 bp.

The Central Bank was active on the market selling over 500 million crowns worth of bonds along the curve as part of its routine financing operations. Dealers said there was sideways trade between the current 10-year bond and the coming benchmark seven percent 2007. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom + 45-33-969650
